questions.q: What is the name of the natural-language-to-SQL assistant built in Project 3?
options: Query Pete
SQL Pete
Northwind Bot
Plan Pete
questions.explain: The assistant is named SQL Pete, scoped to the Northwind and AdventureWorks2012 schemas.

questions.q: Which base model does SQL Pete start from?
options: A 7B+ general-purpose chat model
Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct
A proprietary API-only model
A model trained from scratch for this project
questions.explain: The lab picks Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct: small, open-weight, and code-specialized.

questions.q: Why does SQL Pete need to be open-weight rather than accessed through a closed API?
options: Open-weight models are always more accurate
Closed APIs don't support SQL output
Chapter 5's interpretability case study needs to inspect its internals, which requires the weights
Open-weight models are required by law for research
questions.explain: Chapter 5 reaches into SQL Pete's residual stream for activation patching, which is only possible with full access to the weights.

questions.q: Why does the lab scope SQL Pete to exactly two schemas instead of arbitrary SQL?
options: To bound the table and column vocabulary, making a small base model viable
Because larger schemas are not supported by SQL syntax
Because Northwind and AdventureWorks2012 are the only databases that exist
To avoid using any reward signal at all
questions.explain: Narrowing the task to two known schemas bounds what the model needs to learn, which is what makes a 1.5B model viable.

questions.q: Why does the lab reject a 7B+ base model for this project?
options: 7B+ models cannot generate SQL
It would require multi-GPU training and a slower iteration loop the lab's single-GPU budget and three-stage training plan can't afford
7B+ models are not open-weight
7B+ models are banned from code tasks
questions.explain: A 7B+ model would likely be more fluent, but it doesn't fit single-GPU fine-tuning and would slow down the chapter's three separate training runs.
